extracted.intended_audience: media consumers, journalists, and readers interested in media criticism/fact-checking
extracted.subtask_description: A media-criticism / fact-check article documenting and evaluating a journalist's public claims of reporting from combat zones (specifically Bill O'Reilly's statements about the Falklands). It collects quotations, timelines, and counter-evidence to assess the accuracy and credibility of those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurately state reporting location and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters should correctly and transparently state where they were reporting and their role (e.g., on the islands vs. in a nearby capital like Buenos Aires).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page documents O'Reilly's denials ('I did not say I was in the Falkland Islands.' / 'I was in Buenos Aires ... In Buenos Aires we were in a combat situation after the Argentines surrendered.') alongside numerous prior statements that created the impression he was in a combat zone. Example anti-patterns include claiming to have been 'in the Falklands' when contemporaneous records indicate American reporters were not on the ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not embellish reporting career to imply combat-zone experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should avoid inflating or embellishing their reporting history to create the impression they reported from active combat zones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article's headline and body assert that 'O'Reilly Repeatedly Embellished His Reporting Career To Create The Impression He Reported From A Combat Zone' and then cites multiple quotes across years (e.g., 'I was in a combat situation in Argentina during the Falklands War,' 'I checked the box ... in Falklands War') as examples. These repeated claims are presented as the pattern being criticized; an anti-pattern is repeatedly invoking combat language that is not corroborated by location/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid claiming combat authority to bolster commentary on military matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Public figures and journalists should not assert personal combat experience (or imply it) to claim special authority when commenting on wars, military policy, or veterans' issues unless that experience is factual and appropriately contextualized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: O'Reilly is quoted using combat-related phrasing to justify his authority ('I've seen the combat up close and personal. I didn't have a gun, I had a pen.') and to rebut critics of his commentary on Iran, Iraq, or Afghanistan. The article treats such claims as problematic when they are embellished or not supported by being physically in the combat zone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate claims with contemporaneous evidence and avoid contradicting historical reporting records
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about where and how a journalist reported during historical conflicts should be verifiable against contemporaneous records and other reporting; contradictions undermine credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites Mother Jones' reporting that 'American reporters were not on the ground in this distant war zone' during the Falklands War as a factual counterpoint to O'Reilly's repeated implications of having been 'in a war zone.' Guidance implied: check contemporaneous reporting and records before asserting on-the-ground combat reporting; failure to do so is an anti-pattern that invites fact-checking and criticism.
